cards.front: Recall a key point about Social Stratification & Class
cards.back: Social stratification: the hierarchical arrangement of people into social strata based on wealth, income, status and power. In the UK, social class is the primary form of stratification.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Social Stratification & Class
cards.back: Social class systems: the NS-SEC (8 classes from higher managerial to never worked) replaced the Registrar General's scale. Weber: class is based on market situation. Marx: class is based on relationship to means of production.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Social Stratification & Class
cards.back: Life chances: class strongly affects health (working-class die 7-9 years earlier), education (middle-class children achieve higher), income (top 10% earn 12x more than bottom 10%), and housing (overcrowding 5x higher in lowest quintile).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Social Stratification & Class
cards.back: The wealth gap: richest 10% hold 44% of total wealth; poorest 50% hold 9%. This gap has widened since the 1980s. Wilkinson and Pickett: more unequal societies have worse outcomes for everyone.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Social Stratification & Class
cards.back: Poverty: relative poverty (below 60% of median) affects about 22% of the UK population. The poverty trap: people on benefits who work may be little better off due to lost benefits.

cards.front: What should you know about sociology exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing stratification, always: define the concept, use specific statistics on inequality, and evaluate whether class is still the most important form of stratification.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: According to the ONS, in 2023, approximately 27% of the UK workforce was in NS-SEC Class 1 (professional and managerial), 28% in intermediate occupations, and 45% in routine and manual occupations. However, these proportions vary significantly by region: London has a much higher proportion of Class 1 workers than the North East of England, reflecting the UK’s regional economic inequalities.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: The Social Mobility Commission’s 2023 State of the Nation report found that only 16% of children from working-class backgrounds in the North East of England achieve top GCSE grades, compared to 57% of children from professional backgrounds in London. This 41-percentage-point gap is one of the widest in the developed world.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: In 2023, the Resolution Foundation reported that typical household incomes in the UK were still below their 2019 pre-pandemic levels, the worst performance since the 1950s. Meanwhile, the Sunday Times Rich List showed that the UK’s 350 wealthiest individuals and families had a combined wealth of over £800 billion, an increase of 30% since 2020.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Social class no longer matters because anyone can succeed through talent and hard work. Correct: While social mobility exists, evidence shows class powerfully affects life chances: working-class people die 7-9 years earlier, achieve lower qualifications, earn less. Only 21% of children from the poorest fifth reach the top income quintile as adults. Talent
Evaluate the view that social class is the most significant factor affecting life chances in modern Britain.

cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Social Stratification & Class using sociological terminology accurately. Identify key thinkers, concepts and theoretical perspectives.
